text:
sre-bot: :rotating_light: Incident detected: spike in paged KV cache metadata + continuous-batching increase in eu-west-1. Error rate up 4x on generation RPCs. Auto-notify to #eng-oncall.

lee: seeing sustained blockmgr paging and memory churn on pool gpu-eu-1a. KV metadata objects exploding (~3GB -> 18GB in 20m). Latency cliff around 18:12 UTC, 503s and generator timeouts for some customers.

jordan: confirmed. Continuous batching aggregator went from normal load to huge prefix merges — batch size distribution shifted to long tails. I can reproduce block eviction thrash in staging.

maria: tagging CS/PM. @ash_cs can you flag any live customers?

ash_cs: ACME and NovaApps reporting slow responses, ACME highest QPS on eu-west. They've DM'd support. Severity P1 for customer-impact.

lee: immediate mitigation plan: 1) put runtime into safemode for affected pool (disable continuous batching / set max_batch_size=1) 2) tighten blockmgr eviction policy to aggressive LRU + lower block_size for paged blocks 3) enable prefix KV cache delta sampling to avoid metadata amplification.

jordan: propose rolling this as a canary: apply to 10% of pool nodes, watch tail-latency and metadata growth for 5m, then roll to 50/100. I can push CLI changes.

ravi: i'll own the rollback if anything breaks. prepping a fast-rollback job.

lee: command to flip batching (will run now on pool gpu-eu-1a-canary):
```
redwoodctl runtime update-pool gpu-eu-1a-canary --set continuous_batching.enabled=false --set continuous_batching.max_batch_size=1
```

lee: also applying blockmgr tweak (lower block_size and make eviction aggressive):
```
redwoodctl config patch blockmgr --pool gpu-eu-1a-canary --set block_size_bytes=2097152 --set eviction_policy=aggressive-lru
```

jordan: canary config applied. Observing metrics... metadata growth rate dropped ~60% within 90s. tail P95 latency down from 2.8s -> 1.1s on canary hosts.

maria: getting acknowledgement from ACME: they see much lower error counts on their side. cc @ash_cs

ash_cs: ACME confirms degraded -> normal, thanks. Still seeing a couple of partial responses but overall OK.

lee: rolling to 50% now. executing batch rollout with 30s interval.

jordan: rollout to 50% done. metadata growth stabilized cluster-wide, eviction rate spiked then normalized. No regression in CPU.

ravi: monitor still green. preparing to push to 100%. keep rollback command ready.

lee: rolling to 100%. this should complete in ~6m.

jordan: 100% applied. cluster-level metrics show dropped batch tail and no further paging spikes. Error-rate down to baseline.

maria: handoff notes for next shift: incident caused by sudden change in request shape (long prompt prefixes from a customer A/B test) + a recent autoscaling tweak that removed some batching backpressure. Need postmortem to cover: request-shape protection, batching cap defaults, and blockmgr telemetry.

lee: immediate follow-ups assigned:
- jordan: open hotfix PR to add a runtime flag to auto-limit continuous batching on metadata spike (PR LINK TBD)
- ravi: add canary alert rule for metadata growth > 1GB/5m per pool
- maria: coordinate customer comms with CS, include mitigation timeline
- ash_cs: follow up with ACME onboarding to make sure their A/B test isn't the root cause

jordan: putting a temporary rate-limit on long-prefix requests for eu-west as a protection: `routingctl policy add prefix-length-limit --region eu-west --max-prefix-tokens 2048`

ash_cs: noted. ACME said they started running a batched scoring job at 18:05 UTC that aligns with the spike. investigating.

lee: initial RCA (high level) to be drafted: metadata-amplification from long-prefix batched requests + insufficient guardrails on continuous batching led to massive KV metadata growth and blockmgr paging. We mitigated by disabling continuous batching and tightening eviction.

maria: creating incident ticket and assigning postmortem owner. Will post link when created.

sre-bot: Incident severity: SEV-2 -> downgraded to monitoring after rollback confirmed. Collector: incident-2460012345.

lee: ok closing handoff here. if anyone sees regressions ping this thread. great job on quick canary and rollback. :thumbsup:

jordan: quick note for engineering: let's add a unit test that simulates long-prefix batching hitting paged-kv metadata path. prevented earlier by tests missing long-tail sequences.

maria: handing off to next oncall with context. moving to incident retrospective channel after ticket.

ravi: leaving monitoring alerts for 2h. will update if anything changes.

ash_cs: ACME will keep us posted. thanks all.
